newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, led by silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, led by silver.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Thursday, led a by sharp fall in silver, undermining the recovery of the past ten days, but it is not yet clear that the August-September downtrend has resumed, analysts said.

Fabricators have seen some value around current levels in the past ten days, helping to produce a bounce in precious metals prices, but when the trade bid was withdrawn Thursday, funds were able to sell the market down again on only moderate volumes, traders said.
"The move down began yesterday but a lot of technical damage was done on the charts today," Apostle Capital Management's New Jersey based fund manager Andre Dimino said.

"The rally earlier this month had looked good, encouraging fund shortcovering, and some funds even went net long in silver, but some of those positions look like they have been reversed to a small net short position now," he said.
COMEX December silver ended down 11.8 cents at $4.902 an ounce, after trading down to an eight day low at $4.880.
COMEX December gold closed down 40 cents at $382.60 an ounce, after trading in a $383.20-382.10 range.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $380.35/380.85 an ounce, against the London Thursday afternoon fix of $380.60, and the New York close Wednesday at $380.90/381.40.
Cash market gold is testing the key $380 support level again, dipping to a session low at $379.80 Thursday, and the next major support is seen at the October 1 low at $376.90, analysts said.
Thursday's weakness came despite COMEX gold stocks falling a further 3,044 ounces to 1,054,294 ounces Wednesday, the lowest level since November, 1977.
COMEX silver stocks fell 809,467 ounces Wednesday to 130,794,680, after seeing a ten year low earlier this week.
Silver led the decline in precious metals in September, analysts noted, and led the complex back down again Thursday also.
The spot gold/silver ratio widened to 77.78 at the close, after a decline to 75.4 in the past week, when silver was recovering.
Significant support for silver is now seen around $4.85 in the cash market, a level last reached in late September, before last week's rally began.
NYMEX January platinum ended down 10 cents at $388.20 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium closed down $1.20 at $116.50, after seeing a new December contract low at $116.10.
In the bullion market, physical palladium saw a new three year low at $114.75 an ounce intraday Thursday.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
